materials.summary_zh: 一篇评论性短文：为什么我们自以为擅长同时做几件事，以及“切换成本”如何悄悄降低效率。作者语气带有一定讽刺。（原创文章）

segments.en: Ask a room full of office workers whether they are good at multitasking, and a surprising number will raise their hands with some pride.
segments.zh: 问一屋子上班族是否擅长同时处理多项任务，会有相当多的人略带自豪地举起手。

segments.en: Yet what most of us call multitasking is, strictly speaking, something else: rapidly switching our attention from one task to another.
segments.zh: 然而，我们大多数人所说的“多任务处理”，严格来说是另一回事：把注意力在不同任务之间快速切换。

segments.en: Each switch carries a cost, however small, as the brain has to set aside one set of rules and reload another.
segments.zh: 每一次切换都有成本，无论多小，因为大脑必须放下一套规则，再重新装载另一套。

segments.en: Individually, these costs are barely noticeable; accumulated over a working day, they can add up to a considerable loss of time and accuracy.
segments.zh: 单看每一次，这些成本几乎察觉不到；但在一个工作日里累积起来，就可能造成相当大的时间和准确度损失。

segments.en: What makes the habit so persistent is that it feels productive, since a constant stream of small completed tasks gives us a pleasant sense of momentum.
segments.zh: 这个习惯之所以如此顽固，是因为它让人感觉很高效：源源不断完成的小任务给人一种愉快的推进感。

segments.en: It is precisely this feeling, rather than any measurable result, that keeps us checking messages in the middle of demanding work.
segments.zh: 正是这种感觉，而不是任何可衡量的成果，让我们在做费脑子的工作时还不停地查看消息。

segments.en: Admittedly, some combinations of tasks cause little interference, such as listening to music while running.
segments.zh: 诚然，有些任务组合几乎不会相互干扰，比如边跑步边听音乐。

segments.en: The trouble begins when two activities compete for the same mental resources, as writing a report and answering emails inevitably do.
segments.zh: 问题出在两项活动争夺同一种心理资源的时候，比如写报告和回邮件，这两者必然会相互争夺。

segments.en: The remedy is unglamorous: protected blocks of time, notifications switched off, and the humility to accept that we are not the exception.
segments.zh: 解决办法毫不光鲜：留出不被打扰的整块时间，关掉通知，并谦虚地承认我们并不是例外。

questions.prompt_zh: 作者认为我们所说的“多任务处理”实际上是什么？
options: 在不同任务之间快速切换注意力
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：rapidly switching our attention from one task to another.

questions.prompt_zh: 这个习惯为什么这么难改？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：it feels productive ... a pleasant sense of momentum。下一句强调是这种感觉，而不是可衡量的成果。

questions.prompt_zh: 哪种任务组合几乎不会相互干扰？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：such as listening to music while running.

questions.prompt_zh: “the humility to accept that we are not the exception”暗示了什么？
options: 我们大多数人并不比别人更擅长多任务
我们应该更谦虚地对待同事
少数人确实擅长多任务
questions.explanation_zh: 承认自己不是例外，即承认自己也会受到切换成本的影响。

materials.title_zh: 机器翻译仍然漏掉了什么
materials.summary_zh: 一篇议论文：机器翻译的进步令人惊叹，但作者认为它在语气、言外之意和文化语境上仍有局限，学习外语依然有价值。（原创文章）

segments.en: Not long ago, machine translation was a source of amusement, producing sentences so awkward that they became internet jokes.
segments.zh: 不久以前，机器翻译还是笑料的来源，翻出的句子别扭到成了网络段子。

segments.en: Today the jokes are rarer, and it is tempting to conclude that learning a foreign language has become an expensive hobby.
segments.zh: 如今这样的段子少了，人们很容易就此得出结论：学外语已经成了一种昂贵的爱好。

segments.en: That conclusion, however, rests on a narrow idea of what translation involves.
segments.zh: 然而，这个结论建立在对翻译的狭隘理解之上。

segments.en: Converting the literal meaning of a sentence is only part of the task; the harder part is conveying tone, intention and what is left unsaid.
segments.zh: 转换句子的字面意思只是任务的一部分；更难的是传达语气、意图以及没有说出口的内容。

segments.en: Consider a colleague who writes that your proposal is "certainly ambitious", which may be warm praise or a polite warning, depending on the relationship.
segments.zh: 比如一位同事说你的方案“确实很有雄心”，根据你们的关系，这可能是热情的称赞，也可能是礼貌的警告。

segments.en: A translation can reproduce the words perfectly while missing the warning entirely.
segments.zh: 翻译可以把词完美地复现出来，却完全漏掉其中的警告。

segments.en: Granted, the tools are improving at a remarkable pace, and they are invaluable for reading a menu or a train timetable.
segments.zh: 诚然，这些工具正以惊人的速度进步，在看菜单或火车时刻表时也极其有用。

segments.en: But negotiation, friendship and humour depend on exactly the subtleties that remain hardest to automate.
segments.zh: 但谈判、友谊和幽默恰恰依赖于那些最难以自动化的微妙之处。

segments.en: Moreover, learning a language changes the learner, sharpening their awareness of how meaning is shaped by culture.
segments.zh: 此外，学习一门语言会改变学习者本身，使他们更敏锐地意识到意义是如何被文化塑造的。

segments.en: Far from being obsolete, then, language learning may matter more in an age when anyone can produce a fluent but tone-deaf translation in seconds.
segments.zh: 因此，学外语远没有过时；在任何人都能几秒钟生成流畅却不懂分寸的译文的时代，它可能更加重要。

glossary.zh: 雄心勃勃的；（计划）规模大、难实现的
极其宝贵的（不是“没有价值”）
（比喻）不懂分寸的；对语气不敏感的

questions.prompt_zh: 作者认为“学外语已成昂贵爱好”这个结论有什么问题？
options: 它对翻译的理解太狭隘
它低估了学外语的费用
它高估了机器翻译的速度
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：That conclusion, however, rests on a narrow idea of what translation involves.

questions.prompt_zh: “certainly ambitious”这个例子说明了什么？
options: 同一句话可能是称赞也可能是警告，翻译容易漏掉
同事之间应该直接说话
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：may be warm praise or a polite warning ... A translation can reproduce the words perfectly while missing the warning entirely.

questions.prompt_zh: 作者承认机器翻译在什么方面很有用？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：they are invaluable for reading a menu or a train timetable.

questions.prompt_zh: 作者的最终观点是什么？
options: 学外语没有过时，甚至可能更重要
机器翻译很快会完全取代人工
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：Far from being obsolete, then, language learning may matter more ...

materials.summary_zh: 一段公开讲座节选：讲者解释遗忘曲线、间隔复习和“提取练习”，并回答听众的问题。（原创讲座）

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: Let me start with an uncomfortable fact: within a day, we typically forget a large share of what we've just learned, unless we do something about it.
segments.zh: 先说一个让人不太舒服的事实：一天之内，我们通常会忘掉刚学内容的很大一部分，除非我们采取措施。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: This isn't a flaw in your memory. Forgetting is how the brain decides what is worth keeping.
segments.zh: 这不是你记忆力的缺陷。遗忘是大脑决定什么值得保留的方式。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: What tells the brain that something matters is repeated use, and in particular, use that requires a bit of effort.
segments.zh: 告诉大脑某样东西重要的，是反复使用，尤其是需要花点力气的使用。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: That's why rereading your notes feels reassuring but achieves surprisingly little; the material looks familiar, so you assume you know it.
segments.zh: 所以重读笔记让人安心，效果却出奇地有限：内容看起来眼熟，你就以为自己会了。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: Trying to recall the answer before you look, what researchers call retrieval practice, is far more effective, even when you get it wrong.
segments.zh: 在看答案之前先尝试回忆，也就是研究者所说的“提取练习”，要有效得多，即使你答错了也是如此。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: Timing matters too. Reviewing just as you're about to forget strengthens the memory more than reviewing while it's still fresh.
segments.zh: 时机也很重要。在快要忘记时复习，比在记忆还新鲜时复习更能巩固记忆。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: So the intervals between reviews should grow: a day, then a few days, then a week or more.
segments.zh: 所以复习的间隔应该逐渐拉长：一天，然后几天，然后一周或更久。

segments.speaker: Student
segments.en: Doesn't that mean you'll get more answers wrong, though?
segments.zh: 可这样不就会答错更多吗？

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: It does, and that's rather the point. A slightly difficult review is a productive one; an easy one mostly flatters you.
segments.zh: 是的，而这恰恰是关键。稍有难度的复习才有成效；太容易的复习大多只是让你自我感觉良好。

segments.speaker: Lecturer
segments.en: The practical lesson is to test yourself little and often, and to treat mistakes as information rather than failure.
segments.zh: 实际的启示是：少量多次地自我测试，把错误当作信息，而不是失败。

questions.prompt_zh: 讲者怎么看待遗忘？
options: 是大脑筛选值得保留的信息的方式
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：Forgetting is how the brain decides what is worth keeping.

questions.prompt_zh: 为什么重读笔记效果有限？
options: 内容看着眼熟，让人误以为已经掌握
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：the material looks familiar, so you assume you know it.

questions.prompt_zh: 什么时候复习效果最好？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：Reviewing just as you're about to forget strengthens the memory more ...

questions.prompt_zh: 讲者怎么回应“这样会答错更多”的问题？
options: 承认会，并认为稍有难度的复习才有成效
建议只复习简单的内容
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：It does, and that's rather the point. A slightly difficult review is a productive one.

materials.summary_zh: 一场圆桌讨论：城市规划者和交通经济学家辩论“十五分钟城市”（日常所需都在步行或骑车十五分钟内）是否可行、是否公平。（原创讨论）

segments.speaker: Chair
segments.en: Our topic tonight is the so-called fifteen-minute city, where shops, schools and doctors are all within a short walk or cycle. Ana, why do you support it?
segments.zh: 今晚的话题是所谓的“十五分钟城市”：商店、学校和诊所都在步行或骑车很短的距离内。Ana，你为什么支持它？

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.en: Because most of what people need day to day shouldn't require a car. When it doesn't, streets become quieter, safer and frankly more pleasant to live in.
segments.zh: 因为人们日常所需的大部分东西本不该需要开车。不需要开车时，街道会更安静、更安全，坦白说，也更宜居。

segments.speaker: Chair
segments.en: David, you're more sceptical.
segments.zh: David，你比较怀疑。

segments.speaker: David
segments.en: I am. Granted, the idea sounds attractive, and in dense city centres it largely describes how people already live.
segments.zh: 是的。诚然，这个想法听起来很诱人，而在人口稠密的市中心，它大体上就是人们现有的生活方式。

segments.speaker: David
segments.en: But it doesn't follow that it can be built everywhere. In the suburbs, there simply aren't enough people to support a school and a clinic every few streets.
segments.zh: 但这并不意味着它能在任何地方实现。在郊区，人口根本不足以支撑每隔几条街就有一所学校和一家诊所。

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.en: That's a fair point about density. However, the answer isn't to give up; it's to allow more homes and small businesses in areas that are currently car-dependent.
segments.zh: 关于人口密度，这个观点很合理。但答案不是放弃，而是在目前依赖汽车的地区允许建更多住房和小商户。

segments.speaker: David
segments.en: My other concern is fairness. Neighbourhoods that become pleasant and walkable also tend to become expensive, which can push out the very people they were meant to help.
segments.zh: 我的另一个担忧是公平。变得宜居、适合步行的社区往往也会变贵，这可能把原本想要帮助的人挤出去。

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.en: I don't dispute that risk. Which is precisely why any plan needs affordable housing built in from the start, not added as an afterthought.
segments.zh: 我不否认这个风险。正因为如此，任何方案都必须从一开始就纳入经济适用房，而不是事后补充。

segments.speaker: Chair
segments.en: So you agree on more than it first appeared?
segments.zh: 所以你们的共识比一开始看起来要多？

segments.speaker: David
segments.en: On the goal, yes. Where we differ is how quickly, and how universally, it can realistically be achieved.
segments.zh: 在目标上是的。我们的分歧在于它实际上能多快、多普遍地实现。

glossary.zh: 经济适用房；可负担住房

questions.prompt_zh: Ana 支持“十五分钟城市”的主要理由是什么？
options: 日常所需不该依赖汽车，街道会更安静安全
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：most of what people need day to day shouldn't require a car ... quieter, safer ...

questions.prompt_zh: David 认为郊区难以实现的原因是什么？
options: 人口不够，撑不起密集的学校和诊所
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：there simply aren't enough people to support a school and a clinic every few streets.

questions.prompt_zh: David 的第二个担忧是什么？
options: 宜居社区变贵，把原本要帮助的人挤走
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：tend to become expensive, which can push out the very people they were meant to help.

questions.prompt_zh: 讨论最后，两人的分歧主要在哪里？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：Where we differ is how quickly, and how universally, it can realistically be achieved.

materials.summary_zh: 一篇议论文：城市削减行道树开支是短视的，因为树木的好处真实存在却不在账本上。

segments.en: When city budgets are squeezed, street trees are often among the first casualties: planting is postponed, maintenance is cut, and mature trees are felled to make way for wider roads or new developments.
segments.zh: 城市预算紧张时，行道树往往首当其冲：种植被推迟，养护被削减，成年大树被砍掉，为更宽的道路或新开发项目让路。

segments.en: This treats trees as decoration, a pleasant extra to be funded once the serious spending has been done.
segments.zh: 这是把树木当作装饰，一种等正经开支完成后才去出钱的锦上添花。

segments.en: The evidence suggests otherwise.
segments.zh: 证据表明并非如此。

segments.en: A mature tree can lower the surrounding air temperature by several degrees on a hot day, reduce the load on drains during heavy rain, and filter a measurable share of airborne pollution.
segments.zh: 一棵成年大树在炎热的日子里能让周围气温降低好几度，在暴雨时减轻排水系统的负担，并过滤掉可观比例的空气污染物。

segments.en: Streets with more trees tend to have lower rates of heat-related illness, and some studies have linked green views to faster recovery in hospital patients.
segments.zh: 树木较多的街道，与高温相关的疾病发生率往往较低；一些研究还把看得见绿色景观与住院病人恢复得更快联系起来。

segments.en: None of these benefits appear on a council's balance sheet, which is precisely why they are so easily overlooked.
segments.zh: 这些好处都不会出现在市政府的资产负债表上，而这恰恰是它们如此容易被忽视的原因。

segments.en: The comparison with other infrastructure is instructive.
segments.zh: 与其他基础设施作比较，很有启发意义。

segments.en: No one would suggest delaying the repair of a bridge because the benefits are hard to see; yet a young tree, unlike a bridge, gains value every year it is allowed to grow.
segments.zh: 没有人会因为好处不容易看到而建议推迟修桥；然而，与桥不同，一棵小树每多长一年，价值就增加一分。

segments.en: Cutting it down to save money in the short term is less a saving than a slow and invisible loan taken out against the future.
segments.zh: 为了短期省钱把它砍掉，与其说是节约，不如说是向未来借了一笔缓慢而看不见的贷款。

glossary.note_zh: take out a loan = 借一笔贷款

questions.prompt_zh: 作者认为预算紧张时城市对待行道树的方式说明了什么？
options: 把树当作可有可无的装饰
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：This treats trees as decoration, a pleasant extra.

questions.prompt_zh: 文中提到的成年大树的好处不包括哪一项？
options: 在暴雨时减轻排水负担
questions.explanation_zh: 原文列出了降温、减轻排水负担和过滤空气污染，没有提到税收。

questions.prompt_zh: 为什么这些好处容易被忽视？
options: 它们不会出现在资产负债表上
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：None of these benefits appear on a council's balance sheet, which is precisely why they are so easily overlooked.

questions.prompt_zh: 作者把砍树省钱比作什么？
options: 向未来借的一笔看不见的贷款
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：less a saving than a slow and invisible loan taken out against the future.

materials.title_en: The Placebo That Isn't a Secret
materials.summary_zh: 一篇科普文章：明确告知病人的“开放标签”安慰剂试验，研究结果、局限和启示。

segments.en: For decades, doctors assumed that a placebo works only if the patient believes it is real medicine.
segments.zh: 几十年来，医生们一直认为，只有当病人相信那是真药时，安慰剂才会起作用。

segments.en: Deception, in other words, was thought to be the active ingredient.
segments.zh: 换句话说，欺骗被认为是其中的“有效成分”。

segments.en: A growing body of research has complicated that picture.
segments.zh: 越来越多的研究让这一图景变得复杂起来。

segments.en: In so-called open-label trials, patients are told plainly that the pills they are taking contain no drug at all, yet many still report a noticeable improvement in symptoms such as chronic pain or fatigue.
segments.zh: 在所谓的“开放标签”试验中，病人被明确告知他们服用的药片根本不含任何药物，然而许多人仍然报告诸如慢性疼痛或疲劳等症状有明显改善。

segments.en: Researchers are cautious about what this means.
segments.zh: 研究人员对这意味着什么持谨慎态度。

segments.en: The trials are generally small, and the improvements are mostly in self-reported symptoms rather than measurable changes in the body.
segments.zh: 这些试验规模一般较小，改善大多体现在自我报告的症状上，而不是身体可测量的变化。

segments.en: It is also hard to separate the effect of the pill from that of the attention and care that come with taking part in a study.
segments.zh: 而且很难把药片的作用，与参与研究所带来的关注和照顾的作用区分开来。

segments.en: Still, the findings raise an intriguing possibility: that the ritual of treatment, the act of taking something regularly with the expectation of relief, may matter in its own right.
segments.zh: 尽管如此，这些发现提出了一个耐人寻味的可能性：治疗的仪式感——带着缓解的期望定期服用某样东西的行为——本身可能就有意义。

segments.en: If so, the old ethical dilemma of whether doctors may deceive patients for their own good might be partly avoidable.
segments.zh: 如果是这样，医生能否为了病人好而欺骗病人这个古老的伦理难题，或许在一定程度上是可以避免的。

segments.en: None of this makes placebos a substitute for effective treatment, but it suggests that how medicine is given may deserve as much attention as what is given.
segments.zh: 这一切都不能让安慰剂替代有效的治疗，但它表明，药是怎么给的，可能和给的是什么同样值得关注。

glossary.zh: 开放标签的（病人知道自己服用的是什么）

questions.prompt_zh: 过去医生认为安慰剂起作用的关键是什么？
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：a placebo works only if the patient believes it is real medicine.

questions.prompt_zh: “开放标签”试验的特点是：
options: 病人不知道自己在参加试验
病人被明确告知药片里没有药物
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：patients are told plainly that the pills they are taking contain no drug at all.

questions.prompt_zh: 研究人员为什么持谨慎态度？
options: 试验规模小、改善多为自我报告，且难以排除关注和照顾的作用
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：The trials are generally small … mostly in self-reported symptoms … hard to separate the effect of the pill from that of the attention and care.

questions.prompt_zh: 作者最后的观点是：
options: 安慰剂可以替代大多数药物
医生应该经常欺骗病人
安慰剂不能替代有效治疗，但给药的方式可能同样值得关注
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：None of this makes placebos a substitute … how medicine is given may deserve as much attention as what is given.

materials.summary_zh: 一篇议论文：平台零工的“灵活性”究竟属于谁，作者主张兼顾时间自主和基本保障。

segments.en: Platform companies like to describe the people who deliver our food and drive our taxis as independent entrepreneurs who value flexibility above all else.
segments.zh: 平台公司喜欢把为我们送外卖、开出租车的人描述成把灵活性看得高于一切的独立创业者。

segments.en: There is some truth in this.
segments.zh: 这种说法有一定道理。

segments.en: Surveys consistently show that many workers appreciate being able to choose their own hours, and for students or carers, that freedom can be genuinely valuable.
segments.zh: 调查一致显示，许多劳动者很看重能自己选择工作时间；对学生或需要照顾家人的人来说，这种自由确实很有价值。

segments.en: But flexibility is a curious word for an arrangement in which pay can be cut overnight by an algorithm and accounts can be deactivated without explanation.
segments.zh: 但是，用“灵活”来形容这样一种安排未免奇怪：报酬可能一夜之间被算法削减，账号可能在没有任何解释的情况下被停用。

segments.en: Nor is there any sick pay when a rider is injured on the job.
segments.zh: 骑手工作中受伤，也没有病假工资。

segments.en: In practice, the flexibility often runs in one direction: the company can adjust its demand for labour minute by minute, while the worker absorbs the risk.
segments.zh: 实际上，这种灵活性往往是单向的：公司可以一分钟一分钟地调整对劳动力的需求，而风险由劳动者承担。

segments.en: Courts in several countries have begun to question whether such workers are really self-employed at all.
segments.zh: 好几个国家的法院已经开始质疑，这些劳动者到底算不算真正的自雇者。

segments.en: The companies warn that treating them as employees would destroy the very freedom they enjoy and push up prices for consumers.
segments.zh: 这些公司警告说，把他们当作雇员会毁掉他们所享有的那种自由，并推高消费者的价格。

segments.en: That may be partly true, but it frames the choice too narrowly.
segments.zh: 这也许有部分道理，但它把选择框得太窄了。

segments.en: It ought to be possible to design a model that preserves control over one's hours while guaranteeing a basic floor of income and protection.
segments.zh: 应该有可能设计出一种模式，既保留劳动者对自己工作时间的掌控，又保证最基本的收入和保障底线。

glossary.note_zh: a floor of income = 收入底线

materials.title_en: In Praise of the Quiet Carriage
materials.summary_zh: 一篇随笔：火车上的安静车厢为什么难得，它靠什么维持，又说明了什么。

segments.en: There is a small, unglamorous institution on many trains that deserves more credit than it gets: the quiet carriage.
segments.zh: 许多火车上都有一种不起眼的小设施，它值得的赞誉远比它得到的多：安静车厢。

segments.en: Its rules are modest: no phone calls, no music without headphones, conversation kept to a murmur.
segments.zh: 它的规定很简单：不打电话，不外放音乐，交谈要压低声音。

segments.en: Yet it is one of the few public spaces left in which silence is not merely tolerated but actively protected.
segments.zh: 然而，它是为数不多的、安静不仅被容忍而且被积极保护的公共空间之一。

segments.en: We rarely notice how much of modern life is designed to capture our attention, from the screens in waiting rooms to the music in shops.
segments.zh: 我们很少注意到现代生活中有多少东西是为了抓住我们的注意力而设计的，从候诊室里的屏幕到商店里的音乐。

segments.en: Noise has become the default, and quiet something we must pay for, whether through noise-cancelling headphones or first-class tickets.
segments.zh: 噪音成了默认状态，而安静则成了我们必须花钱买的东西，无论是通过降噪耳机还是头等座车票。

segments.en: The quiet carriage is a rare exception: a shared agreement, available to anyone with an ordinary ticket, that for the length of a journey, attention belongs to the passenger.
segments.zh: 安静车厢是一个罕见的例外：一个任何持普通车票的人都可以享有的共同约定——在旅途中，注意力属于乘客自己。

segments.en: Of course, the agreement is fragile.
segments.zh: 当然，这个约定很脆弱。

segments.en: It depends entirely on strangers being willing to remind one another of the rules, politely and without self-righteousness, which is a surprisingly difficult social skill.
segments.zh: 它完全依赖陌生人愿意互相提醒规则，而且要礼貌、不自以为是——这是一项出奇难的社交技能。

segments.en: But perhaps that is precisely its value: in a small way, it shows that a public good can be maintained by nothing more than mutual consideration.
segments.zh: 但也许这正是它的价值所在：它以一种小小的方式表明，一项公共利益仅靠相互体谅就能维持。
